                    ### Question
                    A 3-year-old male is brought to the ER with a sore throat and fever. Examination of the pharynx reveals a dark, inflammatory exudate. Cysteine-tellurite agar culture produces black, iridescent colonies. Microscopic features of the causal organism most likely include which of the following?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Serpentine growth patterns
opb. Metachromic granules
opc. Lancet-shape
opd. Long, branching filaments
ope. Kidney-bean shaped rod

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The microscopic features of Clostridium diphtheriae infection are lancet-shaped, not kidney-bean shaped rods. The presence of a dark, inflammatory exudate in the pharynx and black, iridescent colonies on cysteine-tellurite agar culture support the diagnosis of diphtheria, with the characteristic microscopic feature being lancet-shaped organisms.
